name: Raleigh
tagline: Research Triangle Excellence with Four Mild Seasons
description: Raleigh sits at the heart of the Research Triangle, surrounded by top-tier universities, world-class healthcare systems, and a thriving tech economy. The cost of living is moderate by East Coast standards, and the city offers four distinct but mild seasons with stunning fall foliage and pleasant springs. For FIRE seekers who value access to excellent medical care, a highly educated community, and a blend of urban amenities with Southern charm, Raleigh is hard to beat.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate to High – safe suburbs; typical metro considerations downtown
quickFacts.climate: Humid subtropical with mild winters, warm summers, and beautiful fall and spring seasons

housing.description: Cheapest-acceptable studio or older 1BR in Southeast Raleigh or near Brier Creek

dining.description: Casual local spots, food trucks, and breweries a few times a week; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: A subsidized Silver plan on North Carolina's ACA marketplace, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600 for a single person; above that, the full price climbs toward $1,000 a month. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance; a car is needed, though some areas are bikeable

entertainment.description: Free state museums downtown by the Capitol, greenway hiking, budget NC State games

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable one-bedroom in Southeast Raleigh or near Brier Creek, cooking most meals at home with food trucks and breweries a few times a week. A paid-off car handles most errands, though parts of the city are bikeable, and proximity to Duke and UNC hospitals means good access even on a budget — with the ACA Silver premium affordable only if annual income stays under the 2026 ~$62,600 subsidy cutoff. The free state museums downtown by the Capitol and the extensive greenway trails fill the calendar, and the mild climate keeps utilities manageable.

housing.description: A decent 1BR in North Hills or a townhome in Cary or Apex

dining.description: Dining out several times a week across the Triangle's growing food scene

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost stays low only if MAGI is managed under the ~$62,600 cliff

transportation.description: A reliable car, full coverage, occasional use of Raleigh's growing transit

entertainment.description: Carolina Hurricanes games, DPAC shows, a gym and museum memberships

2M.lifestyle: A decent one-bedroom in North Hills or a Cary townhome, with dining out several times a week across the Triangle's growing food scene. A reliable car covers trips to the Blue Ridge or Outer Banks, both a few hours away, and there's room for Hurricanes games, DPAC shows, and museum memberships. Good ACA coverage with Duke and UNC systems nearby rounds out comfortable Triangle living.

dining.description: Regular fine dining at Poole's Diner, Death & Taxes, and Second Empire; wine events

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan with Duke and UNC access; padded near the ~$62,600 ACA subsidy cutoff where premium tax credits phase out

transportation.description: A late-model car, premium insurance, weekend trips to the mountains or coast

entertainment.description: Hurricanes season tickets, a golf club, spa visits, museum patron level

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality small home in Five Points or Cameron Village, walkable and tree-lined, with regular dinners at Poole's Diner, Death & Taxes, and Second Empire. Hurricanes season tickets, a golf membership, and premium insurance with Duke and UNC access all fit, with healthcare a Gold plan padded near the ~$62,600 ACA subsidy cutoff. A well-rounded, affluent life in a metro with genuinely strong healthcare infrastructure.

dining.description: Fine dining several nights a week plus a private chef for dinner parties, wine-club memberships

5M.lifestyle: A luxury home in Hayes Barton or a Prestonwood custom build, weekly housekeeping, and concierge medicine with Duke or UNC physicians. Fine dining several nights a week, a luxury car, a country club membership, and Outer Banks weekend getaways are standard, with business-class travel the default. The Triangle's educated community and top-tier medical access make for a very well-supported life.

dining.description: A private chef several days a week, exclusive wine dinners, catered university and charity events

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized concierge practice at Duke or UNC plus specialist access on demand — fully out of subsidy range

transportation.description: A premium vehicle plus regular private car service

entertainment.description: Major university philanthropy, international travel, art patronage, exclusive events

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeping several days a week plus a grounds service

10M.lifestyle: A grand estate in Hayes Barton or a Cary compound with acreage, housekeeping several days a week with a grounds service, and a private chef several days a week, with top-tier concierge care at Duke or UNC and specialist access on demand. First-class travel, a premium vehicle with car service, and regular Outer Banks getaways are all within reach. The Triangle's three research universities and major medical centers anchor a life — roughly $206k a year — where daily costs never register, with room for meaningful philanthropy.
